 Prabowo to Join ASEAN Manila Talks Overshadowed by Haze
 Jayanty Nada Shofa 
 November 11, 2026 | 10:50 pm 
 SHARE 
 URL berhasil di salin.
 President Prabowo Subianto attends the 48th ASEAN Summit in Cebu on May 8, 2026. (Photo Courtesy of Presidential Press Bureau) 
 Jakarta. The government confirmed on Wednesday that President Prabowo Subianto would attend the upcoming ASEAN Summit in Manila, a gathering set to be overshadowed by Indonesia's fire smoke haze. 
 The Philippine capital of Manila will hold the ASEAN Summit from Nov. 16 to 18.
 Southeast Asian leaders are set to sit together to take stock of the group’s internal teamwork. Sessions with ASEAN’s partners, including major powers Beijing and Washington, are on the agenda.
 “President [Prabowo] is scheduled to join the ASEAN Summit in Manila,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Yvonne Mewengkang told reporters in Jakarta on Wednesday.
 ADVERTISEMENT
 She did not go into more detail.
 The gathering, however, will take place against the backdrop of a bad episode of regional haze. Over the past few months, Singapore and Malaysia have struggled to have clear skies due to the toxic smog from Indonesian wildfires. 
 The pollution has led to friction with Singapore that even spiraled into energy security issues and angry rhetoric. 
 The Foreign Ministry had told an earlier presser that Jakarta would encourage ASEAN members to ratify a regional agreement on a haze control center. This Indonesia-based center aims to facilitate better mitigation responses. This agreement, however, requires at least six ASEAN members to ratify before it can enter into force, but so far only Vietnam has done so.
 Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong too will likely head to Manila, although it is unclear if he will hold bilateral talks with Prabowo.
 During a recent Jakarta trip, Singapore's chief diplomat Vivian Balakrishnan said both leaders had communicated and set the political commitment “to do what is necessary”, including on the haze issue. The neighbors agreed to form a joint task force to trace the funds linked to the companies responsible for the forest fires.
 Malaysia has stated it would tap ASEAN channels, while offering Indonesia water-bombing helicopters and personnel.
